disclaimer: Prototype register of notable South African mines compiled from public sources. Coordinates are approximate (see precisionM). Production ranges marked 'low' confidence and all residual figures are modelled estimates that must be replaced with SAMINDABA / DMPR records before operational use.

mines.name: CRD Mine (disused)
mines.notes: 17 Jul 2026: two SANDF members (1 Parachute Battalion) died after falling into an open vertical shaft while pursuing suspected illegal miners during Operation Prosper

mines.name: Crown Mines
mines.notes: Once among the richest gold mines in the world; Riverlea / Zamimpilo illegal-mining raids (2023) on adjacent ground

mines.name: Consolidated Main Reef
mines.notes: Adjacent to Riverlea ground cleared during 2023 operations

mines.name: Langlaagte Estate
mines.notes: Near George Harrison Park, site of the 1886 Main Reef discovery

mines.name: Buffelsfontein Shaft 11
mines.notes: Aug 2024 to Jan 2025 standoff; 78 bodies and 246 survivors recovered in Jan 2025 (87 deaths in total)

mines.name: TGME Pilgrim's Rest
mines.notes: Heritage gold-rush town; illegal mining reported in surrounding adits

mines.name: Durban Roodepoort Deep
mines.notes: Informal settlements on old mine land; surface tailings retreated by DRDGOLD

mines.name: East Rand Proprietary Mines (ERPM)
mines.notes: Angelo informal settlement gas-leak deaths (Jul 2023) linked to illegal gold processing; Central Basin AMD pumping station nearby

mines.name: Buffelsfontein Shaft 10
mines.notes: Linked workings; reports allege bodies remain underground after the 2025 sweep

mines.name: Randfontein Estates
mines.notes: West Rand Basin acid mine drainage decant began 2002

mines.name: Orkney (Pamodzi)
mines.notes: Operator liquidated in 2009; persistent illegal mining in surrounding settlements

mines.name: Cooke Operations
mines.notes: Operator has publicly reported extensive illegal-mining infiltration of Cooke shafts

mines.name: Grootvlei
mines.notes: Collapsed under Aurora Empowerment Systems (2009–2011); infrastructure stripped

mines.name: Stilfontein Gold Mine
mines.notes: Operator collapse in 2005 (Margaret Shaft); long-running illegal mining hotspot

mines.name: Kleinzee
mines.notes: Namaqualand coastal diamond fields: illegal diggers widely reported

mines.name: De Beers Mine
mines.notes: Illegal diggers reported on Kimberley tailings and old workings

mines.name: West Rand Consolidated
mines.notes: West Village (Krugersdorp) attack at abandoned mine dump, Jul 2022, linked to illegal miners

mines.name: Village Main Reef
mines.notes: Early outcrop mine on the Main Reef

mines.name: Marievale
mines.notes: Adjacent to Marievale Bird Sanctuary wetland

mines.name: Robinson Deep
mines.notes: Deep-level Central Rand mine; surface dumps reprocessed

mines.name: City Deep
mines.notes: Deep-level Central Rand mine

mines.name: Transvaal & Delagoa Bay Colliery
mines.notes: Old Witbank workings: spontaneous combustion, subsidence and illegal coal digging

mines.name: Lichtenburg Alluvial Diggings
mines.notes: 1926 Grasfontein diamond rush drew tens of thousands of diggers

mines.name: Sheba
mines.notes: One of the oldest operating gold mines in the world

mines.name: Blyvooruitzicht
mines.notes: Liquidated 2013; heavily mined illegally while dormant; restarted by a new operator

mines.name: Great Noligwa (Vaal Reefs)
mines.notes: Part of the former Vaal Reefs complex

mines.name: Merriespruit
mines.notes: 22 Feb 1994 tailings dam failure killed 17 people

mines.name: Lily Mine
mines.notes: 5 Feb 2016 crown-pillar collapse; three workers in a surface container were never recovered

mines.name: Kopanang
mines.notes: Vaal River operations straddle the NW/FS boundary; position falls on the Free State bank

mines.name: Cullinan (Premier)
mines.notes: Source of the 3 106 ct Cullinan Diamond (1905)

mines.name: South Deep
mines.notes: Large remaining mechanised resource

mines.name: Mponeng
mines.notes: Deepest mine in the world (about 4 km)

mines.name: Masimong
mines.notes: Approaching end of life

mines.name: Jagersfontein
mines.notes: Underground closed 1971; tailings retreatment ended after the 11 Sep 2022 tailings dam failure

mines.name: Moab Khotsong
mines.notes: Vaal River operations straddle the NW/FS boundary; position falls on the Free State bank

mines.name: Venetia
mines.notes: Transitioned from open pit to underground in 2023

mines.name: Voorspoed
mines.notes: Historic workings (1906) re-opened 2008

mines.name: Alexander Bay (Alexkor)
mines.notes: State-owned operator; illegal diamond mining reported along the lower Orange River coast

mines.name: Hlobane Colliery
mines.notes: 12 Sep 1983 methane explosion killed 68 miners

mines.name: O'okiep Copper
mines.notes: Historic copper district mined since the 1850s

mines.name: Kuruman Cape Blue
mines.notes: Crocidolite (blue asbestos) near Kuruman

mines.name: Mafefe Asbestos
mines.notes: Crocidolite; listed derelict asbestos site

mines.name: Penge Asbestos
mines.notes: Amosite (brown asbestos) — severe community health legacy

mines.name: Msauli Asbestos
mines.notes: Chrysotile asbestos

mines.name: Pomfret Asbestos
mines.notes: Crocidolite (blue asbestos); listed derelict asbestos site

mines.name: Marikana
mines.notes: 16 Aug 2012 Marikana massacre: 34 striking mineworkers killed by police

mines.name: Kimberley Mine (Big Hole)
mines.notes: About 22.5 Mt excavated by hand; 2 722 kg (14.5 Mct) of diamonds; now a heritage site

mines.name: Palabora
mines.notes: Open pit deepened to about 760 m before block-cave underground

mines.name: Two Rivers
mines.notes: Steelpoort valley on the Limpopo/Mpumalanga boundary; position falls in Limpopo

mines.name: Coalbrook North Colliery
mines.notes: 21 Jan 1960 pillar collapse killed 435 miners, the worst mining disaster in SA history

mines.name: Prieska Copper
mines.notes: Being redeveloped by a new operator

mines.name: Koegas Asbestos
mines.notes: Crocidolite; partially rehabilitated
